title: Spare part inventory business case
source: spi/db/spi.sqlite via engine batch; prices are last IDR PO item amounts read as unit prices

notes: Estimate: priced materials only, stock counted once per material.
B/C excess and non-moving candidates are unioned by taking the larger eligible quantity for each material, never adding it twice.
S/A non-moving insurance and OEM Max-zero reserves are excluded before any release cohort is formed.
Critical active-stock excess is a separate engineering-review cohort, not approved release.
Estimate: scaled empirical lead-time demand, not a new sampling of lead-time uncertainty.
Stockout cycles per year assumes independent lead-time cycles; not observed annual failures.
Exposure sums part-level scores; shared equipment and correlated losses can overlap. Do not claim this sum as plant downtime loss.
Changing the service target changes target stock; existing-stock risk changes only when stock or demand is changed.
Held insurance reserves are not reduced below one; zero stock is not silently replenished by the baseline scenario.

assumption.rule: campaign month = distinct issue orders at least 1.6 times the median month; future load index = planned items divided by the median of months 4 to 12 of the horizon

campaign.reading: Issue activity shows 2 campaign month(s) in 17: 2025-12, 2026-01. In those months issues ran 2.8 times the normal month across every item type. The maintenance plan puts 1123 planned items in 2026-10 against a run rate of about 310 per month later in the horizon (Estimate: next due dates are calculated from cycle starts).

replay_limitations: Estimate, not achieved service: current stock snapshot is a common initial condition; constant lead time is estimated on complete history; dynamic parameters fitted on full history. Monthly lost-sales replay has no observed receipts; do not claim a causal or out-of-sample service improvement.

limitations: Gross excess is not immediately recoverable cash. Max 0 on OEM parts is not permission to dispose.
The top ten parts dominate static excess; validate their prices, interchangeability, ownership and strategic purpose first.

The base case is a B/C stock-keeping pilot; full recommended replenishment can cost more than the reduction candidate ceiling; no positive cash ROI is claimed without evidence of operational benefits.
Avoided downtime and emergency spend are zero until independently substantiated; part-level model exposures overlap and are not monetised as actual plant losses.
The 22% economic carrying indicator is not added to cash NPV; the 4% cash storage rate excludes financing cost to avoid double counting capital release.
